Take consistently with respect to food (food markedly increases absorption)
Avoid; anti-androgenic - risk of feminization of male fetus

summary: Spironolactone is a competitive aldosterone (mineralocorticoid receptor) antagonist that promotes sodium and water excretion while retaining potassium, acting as both a potassium-sparing diuretic and antihypertensive. It improves survival in NYHA class III-IV heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and is used for resistant hypertension, edema of cirrhosis and nephrotic syndrome, and primary hyperaldosteronism. Its principal danger is hyperkalemia, and its anti-androgenic effects cause gynecomastia.
indications: NYHA class III-IV heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (to increase survival, manage edema, reduce hospitalization)
Add-on therapy for hypertension to lower blood pressure
Edema of cirrhosis and of nephrotic syndrome unresponsive to fluid/sodium restriction and other diuretics
Primary hyperaldosteronism - short-term preoperative treatment and long-term maintenance when surgery is not appropriate
Off-label: resistant hypertension, hirsutism/acne (anti-androgen), female-pattern hair loss

dosage.d: 25 mg once daily if K <=5.0 mEq/L and eGFR >50; may increase to 50 mg once daily if tolerated
dosage.n: If eGFR 30-50 consider 25 mg every other day; reduce to 25 mg QOD if hyperkalemia

dosage.d: 25-100 mg daily in single or divided doses
dosage.n: Allow ~2 weeks for full antihypertensive effect

dosage.d: 100 mg daily in single or divided doses (range 25-200 mg)
dosage.n: Initiate in hospital and titrate slowly

dosage.d: 100-400 mg daily preoperatively; lowest effective dose for long-term maintenance
Consider 25 mg every other day initial; avoid if severe impairment

admin: Can be taken with or without food but should be taken consistently with respect to meals
In heart failure, generally discontinue potassium supplements when starting spironolactone
Recheck serum potassium when ACE inhibitor/ARB therapy is changed
Titrate edema/HF doses slowly and monitor for hyperkalemia
Counsel that gynecomastia/breast tenderness may occur and is usually reversible
moa: Spironolactone and its active metabolites are specific competitive antagonists of aldosterone at the mineralocorticoid receptor of the aldosterone-dependent sodium-potassium exchange site in the distal renal tubule. This increases excretion of sodium and water while sparing potassium, producing diuresis and lowering blood pressure. It also blocks androgen receptors and inhibits steroidogenesis, accounting for anti-androgenic effects such as gynecomastia.

absolute: Anuria / acute renal failure (significant impairment of renal excretory function)
relative: Concomitant potassium supplements or potassium-sparing agents
monitor: Concomitant ACE inhibitors, ARBs, NSAIDs, trimethoprim, heparin (hyperkalemia)

preg: Based on mechanism and animal data, spironolactone may impair sex differentiation of the male fetus (feminization). Limited human data have not clearly shown major malformations, but because of the anti-androgenic risk, avoid spironolactone in pregnancy or counsel a pregnant woman about the potential risk to a male fetus.
lact: Spironolactone's active metabolite canrenone is excreted in breast milk. Use with caution while breastfeeding; if a diuretic is required, an alternative may be preferred and the infant monitored.
renal: Renal impairment markedly increases the risk of hyperkalemia. Reduce dose/frequency (e.g. 25 mg every other day) when eGFR is 30-50 mL/min/1.73 m2 and avoid in severe impairment or anuria. Monitor potassium and renal function closely.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment and cirrhosis; spironolactone metabolism may be altered and electrolyte/acid-base disturbances can precipitate hepatic encephalopathy. Reversible coma has occurred in cirrhotic patients with ascites.

major: Potassium supplements / potassium-containing salt substitutes - severe hyperkalemia
ACE inhibitors and ARBs - additive hyperkalemia (check potassium when therapy changes)
Eplerenone and other potassium-sparing diuretics - contraindicated/dangerous hyperkalemia
Lithium - reduced renal clearance and risk of lithium toxicity
moderate: NSAIDs - reduce diuretic/antihypertensive effect and increase hyperkalemia and renal risk
Trimethoprim (incl. co-trimoxazole) and heparin/LMWH - additive hyperkalemia
minor: Acetylsalicylic acid - may reduce spironolactone efficacy
interactions.food: Food substantially increases bioavailability; take consistently with respect to meals.
interactions.alcohol: Alcohol may increase the risk of orthostatic hypotension; limit intake.
interactions.diagnostics: Interferes with radioimmunoassays of digoxin (falsely altered levels); may raise serum potassium and lower sodium.

serious: Impaired neurologic function/coma in cirrhotic patients
rare: Stevens-Johnson syndrome / toxic epidermal necrolysis / DRESS
emergency: Life-threatening hyperkalemia (weakness, paralysis, peaked T waves, arrhythmia, cardiac arrest)

monitoring: Serum potassium within 1 week of initiation/titration, then regularly (more often with other hyperkalemia-causing drugs or renal impairment)
Renal function (creatinine, eGFR) and volume status
Serum sodium, other electrolytes, uric acid and blood glucose periodically
Signs of gynecomastia and, in cirrhotics, mental status
counsel: Do not use potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless told to
Report muscle weakness, fatigue, slow or irregular heartbeat (signs of high potassium)
Breast swelling/tenderness can occur and is usually reversible after stopping
Take consistently with regard to meals and keep blood-test appointments
Avoid pregnancy; use effective contraception and tell your doctor if pregnant
pk: Diuretic effect builds over 2-3 days; antihypertensive effect over up to 2 weeks
Spironolactone ~2.6 h; active metabolite canrenone ~4.3 h
Parent ~1.4 h; active metabolites (canrenone, TMS, HTMS) ~14-17 h
Effect persists due to long-acting active metabolites
Store at controlled room temperature; protect from light
pearls: Hyperkalemia is the dose-limiting and potentially lethal effect - check potassium within 1 week of starting or titrating and avoid added potassium
Adding spironolactone to ACE inhibitor/ARB in heart failure (RALES) improves survival but mandates strict potassium monitoring
Gynecomastia is dose- and duration-related; eplerenone is a more selective alternative with fewer anti-androgenic effects
Food roughly doubles bioavailability - advise consistent dosing relative to meals
Spironolactone interferes with digoxin immunoassays - interpret digoxin levels with caution
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember the same day; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your usual schedule. Do not take two doses at once. Avoid late-evening dosing to reduce night-time urination.
overdose: Acute overdose may cause drowsiness, confusion, rash, nausea, vomiting, dizziness or diarrhea; hyperkalemia (especially with renal impairment), hyponatremia and, in severe liver disease, hepatic coma can occur. There is no specific antidote. Treat supportively with maintenance of hydration, electrolyte balance and vital functions; manage hyperkalemia actively and discontinue spironolactone if renal impairment is present.
